📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A man in Denver has found a cheap way to beat Waymo’s self-driving system: a few orange traffic cones and a carton of eggs.
  • Waymo states it has counted at least 30 egg attacks on its robotaxis in Denver, all believed to be the same man.
  • It has been revealed that the method is laid out in a Denver police report filed last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man in Denver has found a cheap way to beat Waymo’s self-driving system: a few orange traffic cones and a carton of eggs.

Waymo states it has counted at least 30 egg attacks on its robotaxis in Denver, all believed to be the same man. And the Denver District Attorney’s Office has declined to file charges, calling it a civil matter, according to The Newly introduced York Times.

It has been revealed that the method is laid out in a Denver police report filed last month. The man pulls up in front of a Waymo somewhere in or around downtown, takes orange cones out of his trunk, and sets them around the robotaxi so it can’t drive off. Then come the eggs, sometimes thrown from his driver’s seat, sometimes after he gets out.

He leaves in a silver Toyota Corolla. Per the report, that car belongs to a fleet leased out to Lyft drivers. The man hasn’t been identified, and Lyft didn’t comment.

A Waymo investigator took seven of the incidents to police. Each egged vehicle had to come out of service for cleaning, and the detailing bill came to about $2,000. No permanent damage.

Police brought their findings to prosecutors, who decided “no criminal charges” were appropriate. A spokesperson for the DA told the Times the office is now collecting evidence on potential damage and will work with the city attorney to find “the most appropriate legal mechanism to make this behavior stop.”.

In a recent development, at least one Waymo had a rider inside. Jeff Hunley was headed to the Union Station neighborhood in September when his robotaxi got hit. He filmed it, remarked he felt safe in the car, and got his fare refunded.

Waymo opened its Denver service to the public on September 1, alongside San Diego and Tampa. The company now runs more than 100 vehicles across 60 square miles of the city, and Mayor Mike Johnston is a fan. He called them popular and affordable, and couldn’t resist adding that “overall they’re a good egg.”.

In a recent development, the rest of November hasn’t been as friendly. California’s DMV ordered Waymo’s driverless vehicles off state freeways on November 11 after robotaxis drove into active construction zones and one tried to get past a CHP traffic break. Waymo responded by pausing freeway rides in every US market.

Recent findings suggest that and vandalism isn’t latest for Waymo. We covered it when at least five of its I-Pace robotaxis were set on fire during protests in Los Angeles last year.

Industry observers note that putting a single cone on a Waymo’s hood to freeze it has been a known trick since San Francisco activists did it in 2023. Ringing the car with cones works for the same reason: the Waymo Driver is built to respect them, and it won’t push through.

Industry observers note that A human driver getting pelted with eggs would just roll over a cone and leave. A robotaxi sits there and takes it.

Industry observers note that that’s the correct default. You don’t want a driverless car deciding when a cone is optional, especially two weeks after regulators pulled Waymo off California freeways for ignoring work zones. But it means anyone with a trunk full of cones can pin a robotaxi in place for as long as they want.

We’ll try to keep the egg puns to a minimum. Mostly.

This is small-time vandalism. Two grand in cleaning, no injuries, no lasting damage. But it reveals a real weakness in robotaxis: they’re designed to be the most cautious car on the road, and a determined person can turn that caution against them in under a minute. The car can’t escape, can’t honk its way out, and apparently can’t stop the same guy from coming back 30 times.

The DA’s call is hard to follow. Prosecutors have a repeat pattern, a vehicle tied to a known fleet operator, rider video, and robotaxis that are basically rolling camera rigs. And still no charges. If someone boxed in a regular taxi with a passenger inside and started throwing things at it, we suspect the answer would be different.

At the same time, I can’t help but respect the guy’s dedication.

A Used Cybertruck Is Selling A Month Faster Than A Ford F-150

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet.
  • According to recent reports, the data from the upcoming iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla unveiled it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027.
  • Industry observers note that the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you had to guess which used pickup found a buyer fastest in October, the Toyota Tacoma would be a sensible bet. It’s America’s best-selling midsize truck and has a reputation for holding its value. Or you might pick the super frugal Ford Maverick Hybrid. But the truck that beat them both was the Tesla Cybertruck.

According to recent reports, the data from the upcoming iSeeCars study covers 1.1 million used vehicles that changed hands in October, so this was before Tesla unveiled it would discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027. The study looked at one- to five-year-old vehicles and ranked models by how long they’d been listed before selling.

Industry observers note that the Cybertruck surpassed all other pickups, averaging 39.1 days, compared to 65.5 days for used pickups overall. The Maverick Hybrid came closest at 43.3 days, followed by the Rivian R1T at 45.2 and the F-150 Lightning at 47.4. The Tacoma came in fifth position.

Sources indicate that the gap between the two electric pickups at either end of the list was even more striking. A used Chevrolet Silverado EV took 107.5 days to sell, putting it last among the 24 trucks in the study. That’s a 68-day difference between two American electric pickups. Across the wider used market, EVs averaged about 46 days to find a buyer, around nine fewer than hybrids and 15 fewer than gas vehicles.

It has been revealed that how swiftly a used Cybertruck sold seems to have changed a lot since May 2024, when some sellers were cutting as much as $30,000 from their asking prices after listing their trucks for close to $200,000. By December of that year, we reported that used Cybertrucks were piling up on dealer lots, with data at the time showing they stayed for 75 days, up from 27 in May.

Then owners got a look at what Tesla itself would pay for a used Cybertruck trade-in. One year later, in May 2025, one owner of a $99,990 dual-motor Foundation Series truck got a trade-in estimate of $65,400 after driving it just 6,211 miles.

So even though the Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used pickup in iSeeCars’ fresh study, it didn’t report what buyers paid, so we don’t know whether owners got their asking price or had to lower it to sell.

Tesla will build the last Cybertrucks at the end of summer 2027, and this will reshape their used market. Elon Musk originally announced production would end around the middle of the year, but then extended the run to fill more orders. And if you order a Cybertruck now, the only one you can get is the $110,000 tri-motor Cyberbeast, so anyone who wants a less expensive dual-motor truck has to look for a used example.

Recent findings suggest that once the last new Cybertruck is sold, I’d expect collectors and everyday truck buyers to look at used ones differently. Someone after a clean Foundation Series truck with low miles might pay a little extra for one close to home, especially since it could be months before another comes up for sale nearby.

According to recent reports, at the same time, someone who just needs an electric pickup to tow a trailer has more options. If a used dual-motor Cybertruck costs about the same as a Ford F-150 Lightning or a Rivian R1T, I suspect that buyer will care more about mileage, condition, and how much battery warranty is left than when Tesla built its last truck.

10 Games That Will Feel Better To Play After GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're like 32.5 million other people around the world, you've probably been dedicating a huge amount of time to GTA 6 lately, and you can't imagine what your life will be like when the experience is over.
  • Recent findings suggest that all good things must come to an end, and eventually, your time in Leonida will reach a conclusion.
  • Titles like this one help you appreciate the craft of video game development more than ever, as they fully exploit many of the aspects that make the interactive industry the most special of all those focused on entertainment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're like 32.5 million other people around the world, you've probably been dedicating a huge amount of time to GTA 6 lately, and you can't imagine what your life will be like when the experience is over.

Recent findings suggest that all good things must come to an end, and eventually, your time in Leonida will reach a conclusion. However, crossing that frontier doesn't necessarily have to be a bittersweet farewell but rather an opportunity to re-evaluate everything that comes next.

Titles like this one help you appreciate the craft of video game development more than ever, as they fully exploit many of the aspects that make the interactive industry the most special of all those focused on entertainment.

Therefore, if these hypermodern times have already gotten to you and are making you nervous about what will come after Jason and Lucia's story, calm your anxiety by checking out this list of ten games that will feel better to play after GTA 6.

If you're wondering how on earth this list is going to start with one of the games most diametrically opposed to the philosophy of GTA 6, like GRIS, the answer lies precisely in that statement.

After an adventure brimming with stimuli, endless possibilities, lengthy explanations, and violence that ranges from the personal to the systemic, what better way to unwind than with one of the most focused and introspective titles ever conceived?

In just three hours, without a single word and in a straightforward manner, GRIS takes you on a soothing path of reflection, making peace with the circumstances, and reveling in an audiovisual experience that engulfs you to the point of baptizing you with its art.

Without bullets or socioeconomic problems that dictate your relationship with the law, but with platforms, elegance, and a creative intent so distinct that you won't be able to help but fall in love by the time the credits roll on the Sunday afternoon it takes to complete it.

The cliché of "best game ever" versus "best game today" strikes me as both amusing and illogical, but I do believe there's some value in considering The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake in light of GTA 6.

Both titles excel in their focus on player freedom, yet while GTA achieves this within a stunning range of action that opens up numerous possibilities, Ocarina of Time Remake does so in a much more concentrated and whimsical way.

The charm lies not in the immeasurable variety of options, but in the immeasurable creativity of the single alternative they offer for each sequence, demonstrating in the process how the notion of agency has evolved over the last 30 years.

They are two ends of the same spectrum, and experiencing the same sense of enjoyment through discovery in such different ways is what makes them complement each other far better than you might initially imagine.

Having spent its entire existence in the shadow of Rockstar's work, returning to Saints Row 2 now that GTA has taken a 180-degree turn in its approach has become more fitting than ever.

Jason and Lucia face a more realistic, weighty world with consequences, masterfully encouraging restraint and attention to detail, breaking the connection that pitted the two franchises against each other for so long.

Hence, whether you're among those who didn't fully embrace the change in philosophy or those who did, Saints Row 2's humor and arcade style are a perfect fit to reduce the pleasurable cortisol rush produced by GTA 6.

Don't get me wrong: I greatly appreciate Rockstar's courage in going against its own trend, though that doesn't mean I'm not much more eager to play a more relaxed game once I decide to stop wandering around Leonida, postponing saying goodbye.

After GTA 6, it's quite clear the developer has mastered every imaginable variation of the driving genre, which includes the adrenaline-fueled and spectacular style they employed during the Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition era.

The fact that the vehicles in their latest product had to prioritize accuracy and composure was necessary to fit the rest of the game's structure, yet the primal thrill of getting behind the wheel and flying at 300 kilometers per hour in the most improbable way possible was sacrificed.

Consequently, even considering that the genre as a whole is today much closer to realistic simulation than arcade driving, dusting off your copy of Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition after GTA 6 would be in the instruction manual if GTA 6 had one.

Neither approach is inherently better than the other, evidently, but the desire to truly revel in the speed instead of worrying about the cost of a crash will grow stronger on you with each passing second.

Years go by, and it's incredible how no third-person shooter has understood that they are morally obligated to look to Vanquish to understand how to keep the genre from perpetually stagnating.

Gunfights in GTA 6 are technically impressive and an absolute marvel in terms of action sequences, and yet there isn't a second that goes by that I don't think of Sam Gideon and the thunderous perfection of his combat performance.

Instead of being a turn-based confrontation where both sides take turns behind a wall to exchange bullets, Vanquish is a spiral of destruction that doesn't even stop to reload, presenting a striking contrast to the game we're discussing here.

Sources indicate that would being able to slide at full speed and defeat giant robots in GTA 6 make sense? No. Am I dying to play through Vanquish for the thirtieth time for every occasion I have to stay put in cover? Absolutely.

While this might sound utterly personal, few things please me as much as revisiting a developer's older games after a long time, which brings us to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

Being the franchise's installment I've sunk the most hours into and the reason I love open-world games, it creates an intrinsic incentive for GTA 6 because it allows you to appreciate the passage of time.

Many of the gameplay concepts we enjoy in the franchise today, such as character customization, routines, and minigames, were pioneered by CJ, and taking a step back to appreciate what San Andreas did over 20 years ago is magical.

This recommendation might be harder to justify theoretically because, generally speaking, GTA 6 is a vastly superior version, though the magic of nostalgia is something it won't acquire for another couple of decades, while San Andreas has plenty of that.

Rockstar did an exceptional job, like few developers in history, of truly discouraging lethal attacks through a bloody, sensitive, and visceral presentation, though it's ironic that these same qualities are what elevate DOOM Eternal.

Being careful with how you drive or which body parts you shoot is excellent, but I'd be lying if I didn't admit that a part of me misses the raw brutality with which you can manipulate the Doom Guy to commit hellish extermination.

The two titles contrast sharply in both their approach to combat and the ease of movement that enables it, so just thinking about DOOM Eternal's levels, flying all over the place while leaping from execution to execution, makes my mouth water.

Furthermore, being able to shoot an enemy entity in the face with a shotgun without being completely dismayed by my own lack of humanity is a significant bonus, because I do miss being able to disconnect from the consequences of my characters' actions.

GTA 6 is a game of distance, in the sense that its experience focuses heavily on trajectories, the separation between spaces, and the distinct biomes, doing everything Yakuza 0 refuses to do despite also being an open world.

Kamurocho and Sotenbori occupy a tiny fraction of Leonida's map, and there's no vehicle other than your own two feet to traverse them, though this allows you to connect with every back alley and building in a way that no other title has been able to instill in me.

That familiarity and closeness with which Yakuza 0 relates to its inhabitants, locations, and activities is invaluable, and although GTA 6 manages to generate identical emotions, the difference in scale creates an impressive sense of belonging to Kiryu and Majima's journeys.

There are many points of convergence, but the size breaks down the comparison, allowing their divergences to become apparent as the hours pass, thus highlighting the asymmetries that each offers to fans of the genre.

It's clear after just a couple of hours of gameplay that Red Dead Redemption 2 is the primary influence on GTA 6, so we can all agree that we wouldn't be here if it weren't for Red Dead Redemption.

Replacing the noise of neon lights and social media with horses and forests is something Arthur Morgan's game could easily do, but what even the legendary outlaw can't achieve is to also hark back to a time when even design was more contemplative.

Unlike its sequel, Red Dead Redemption is a prototype whose full expression was prevented by technological limitations, resulting in a much quieter, more poetic, and simpler journey, but with the hints of grandeur that its direct and spiritual successor would achieve in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

Therefore, riding back through its empty landscapes, conversing with its few interactive characters, and firing its limited guns is the handbrake for the Pegassi Vitello inside which we find ourselves in GTA 6, letting us breathe fresh air and appreciate the beauty of slower times.

If at any point between 2013 and now you had told me that GTA 6 would be much more like Shenmue than any other video game, I would have thought you needed a psychiatrist, but here we are.

If you're surprised by the attention to detail in drinking a beverage, observing the routines of dozens of NPCs, having to stay fit and healthy, or enjoying complex minigames, let me inform you that Yu Suzuki was already doing it all back in 1999.

While Shenmue is more similar to Yakuza 0 in scale, it also resembles GTA 6 in that both embrace a life simulation design, where walking, talking, playing, interacting, and other such actions aren't driven by the sheer volume of fun but rather by the experience of placing yourself in someone else's shoes.

That talent for immersing you in a reactive, living world that transcends your existence is reserved for the legends, and if you can tolerate the difference in technological advancement and size, Shenmue will easily show you why it feels like a great-great-grandfather of GTA 6.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that these days, I’m particularly interested in cars of the past.
  • The Patent Motorwagen gets credit for being first because Carl Benz designed it to be a car from the get-go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the November/December 2026 glitch of Car and Driver.

Industry observers note that these days, I’m particularly interested in cars of the past. By that I mean the distant past. Such is the case for the 1886 Benz Patent Motorwagen I drove during Monterey Car Week. Now when someone asks, “What’s the oldest car you’ve ever driven?” I have an unassailable answer. That is, unless you’ve driven Cugnot’s steam car. You did? No way. Was it cool?

The Patent Motorwagen gets credit for being first because Carl Benz designed it to be a car from the get-go. He didn’t simply take a horse-drawn carriage, add an engine and drivetrain, subtract the horse and reins, carry the oats.

I love primordial stuff because things we take for granted today had not yet been figured out. There were lots of guesses—some right, others not. Driving a vehicle that old is disorienting, challenging, and sometimes dangerous. Maybe something will explode. Maybe you’ll fall out. Boring hadn’t been engineered into the experience yet.

See all results for used cars for sale near 53095.

The Patent Motorwagen gives major perambulator vibes, and baby, I am here for it. It has only three wheels, to keep it simple and light. Carriages turned their entire axle, since uprights and kingpins at the wheels were still years away. Steering the first car involves grabbing what appears to be the wood handle of an awl—the automotive steering wheel hadn’t been invented yet either. Also not in existence in 1886: carburetor jets, engine radiators, radios, tetanus shots.

Another hitherto unimagined concept: hiding the crankshaft and flywheel behind casings. The crank, connecting rod, cam gear, and drive belt all sit out in the open. Some of those parts have to be greased up before your drive. For others, oil is metered out onto the cylinder and the intake valve by drip lubricators before it runs over less critical parts and leaves behind a greasy trail on the road.

To start the Benz, switch on the ignition that sends energy to the roughly eight-inch-long spark plug, then grab the horizontal flywheel. Give that a Wheel of Fortune–worthy spin and wait. The air-hexane fuel mixture is adjustable, so you can richen it to help the car start (it originally ran on naphtha, which was available at apothecaries in 1886, right next to the laudanum). There’s no throttle, so the 1.0-liter doesn’t stray far from its 400-rpm operating speed. A 4.8-quart copper vessel perched over the engine holds the water that cools the cylinder. After about an hour of operation, the water boils over, and you stop and take a calf’s-head-stew break to let things cool.

Industry observers note that to accelerate, push the long lever on the left side of the leather-trimmed park bench to engage the engine-driven leather strap to the axle. Feel the 0.88 horsepower. To stop, pull that lever back to actuate a shoe that drags on the axle. Not to sound like an 1886 infomercial, but driving the Patent Motorwagen is so easy, a toddler could do it. It’ll hit a claimed 13 mph, and it was the most amazing 13 mph I’ve ever experienced. There’s no way I’m going to be this fun when I’m 140 years old.

See all results for used cars for sale near 53095.

Senior features editor Elana Scherr shares my fondness for the supercentenarian set. She owns a 1915 Dodge, making her the perfect person to organize a U.S. equivalent of Britain’s London-to-Brighton race for early cars. I rode along and got to exceed a 45-mph speed limit in a 116-year-old Pullman, ancient proof that speed limits are set too low. Not to worry, I was running Waze. Scherr’s account begins on page 64.

Recent findings suggest that if you aren’t in the mood to go antiquing, there’s a 795-hp Mustang on page 34, a nearly 1000-hp Audi super car on page 58, and the fresh Corvette Grand Sport on page 72. Encompassing both new and old, this is a great issue.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

Sources indicate that we’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one newly introduced map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

It has been revealed that while we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a newly introduced matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Industry observers note that things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a latest Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

According to recent reports, interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map upgrade during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another latest Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an patch to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

In a recent development, finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

America is building just 10% of the power lines it needs, experts warn

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that america's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up.
  • Sources indicate that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission.
  • America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that america's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up. More electric vehicles, increased electricity use in heavy industry, and the explosive growth of data centers are driving demand higher, putting additional pressure on an infrastructure system that is already falling behind.

Sources indicate that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission. The problem could have major consequences for electricity prices, grid reliability, and the nation's economic future.

America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.

Industry observers note that A major concern is the extremely slow pace of transmission construction. Over the past five years, the continental United States has added an average of only about 500 miles of high-voltage transmission lines annually. Research suggests the country needs approximately 5,000 miles each year to triple the size of its interregional transmission network by 2050 and accommodate future electricity demand.

In a recent development, that means the U.S. is building new high-voltage transmission lines at just one-tenth of the estimated pace needed.

Sources indicate that high-voltage transmission lines serve as the highways of the electricity system, carrying large amounts of power over long distances from generating facilities to communities and businesses. Connecting regional grids allows electricity to flow more easily between areas, helping balance supply and demand when local power production falls short.

According to recent reports, studies have shown that larger, better-connected electricity networks can reduce costs for consumers while also lowering the risk of catastrophic blackouts. When one region experiences a power shortage, electricity from another region can help keep the lights on.

Despite these advantages, expanding the nation's transmission infrastructure has proved extraordinarily difficult.

The Biggest Obstacle Isn't Technology.

According to the researchers (Madeline Yozwiak, David G. Victor, and M. Granger Morgan), the main barriers to modernizing America's power grid are political and regulatory rather than technological.

Responsibility for approving major transmission projects is divided among federal agencies, state governments, local authorities, and private companies. Each has its own priorities and interests, creating numerous opportunities for proposed power lines to be delayed or blocked.

Existing electric utilities can also have financial reasons to resist stronger connections between regions. Greater competition from electricity suppliers elsewhere could weaken their influence over local markets, reducing the incentive to support projects that would benefit the broader electricity system.

As a result, even transmission projects that could lower costs and improve reliability across the country can struggle to gain approval.

Three Ways to Fix America's Power Grid Crisis.

To address the growing shortfall, the researchers recommend a three-part strategy combining stronger government action, modern transmission technologies, international cooperation, and regulatory reform.

According to recent reports, 1. Make better use of existing federal powers and advanced technologies.

It has been revealed that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and the Department of Energy (DOE) already have legal authorities that could help move important transmission projects forward. The researchers argue that these agencies should use those powers more effectively, including identifying transmission corridors of national importance and addressing disputes that prevent projects from receiving state-level approval.

Industry observers note that technological improvements could also dramatically increase the amount of electricity the grid can carry. One approach, known as reconductoring, involves replacing existing power line conductors with more advanced materials capable of transmitting more electricity without necessarily requiring entirely fresh routes.

Other advances, including newer High-Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) systems, offer additional ways to move large amounts of electricity efficiently. The researchers suggest that modern transmission technologies could double or even triple capacity.

Underground high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables offer another promising option. These systems can carry substantial amounts of electricity over long distances and could potentially be installed along existing highways and railroad corridors. Using these established routes could help avoid some of the land-use disputes and approval challenges that often delay conventional transmission projects.

Industry observers note that 2. Learn from countries that have already overcome similar obstacles.

The United States trails several international counterparts in building long-distance HVDC infrastructure and coordinating electricity transmission across regional and national boundaries.

It has been revealed that other countries have demonstrated that large transmission projects can move forward despite complicated political approval processes. Some have also successfully deployed underground HVDC systems on a large scale.

Rather than developing every solution independently, the researchers suggest that the U.S. should study these international experiences and adapt approaches that have already proved successful.

Industry observers note that one proposal is to establish an international forum involving electricity regulators and other experts, potentially led by organizations such as the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC). Such a forum could help American policymakers identify effective regulatory practices, planning strategies, and technologies used elsewhere.

3. Create a national commission to break the political deadlock.

The researchers also recommend establishing a Presidential-Congressional Transmission Commission to address the political and regulatory conflicts that have slowed grid expansion for decades.

Modeled on previous successful bipartisan commissions, the proposed group would bring together key stakeholders to negotiate difficult decisions and develop a coordinated proposal for reform.

Its responsibilities would include recommending changes to state and federal laws, examining whether FERC should receive broader authority over the locations of latest transmission projects, and developing financial incentives for companies that lead new construction.

The commission could also recommend financial rewards for communities that host transmission infrastructure, helping ensure that local residents share in the benefits of projects that serve larger regions.

Why America's Power Grid Crisis Could Get Worse.

Industry observers note that the researchers emphasize that the underlying challenge is not a lack of engineering solutions. Instead, the country's divided decision-making system allows individual stakeholders to obstruct projects that could deliver substantial nationwide benefits.

"The fundamental challenge isn't technical, it's jurisdictional. Authority is divided among federal, state, and private entities, each with distinct priorities. When every stakeholder possesses the power to say no, even high-value projects that benefit the entire nation struggle to move forward," the authors warn.

Their assessment suggests that simply continuing with the existing system of overlapping regulations and fragmented authority will not be enough to meet America's growing electricity needs.

Without meaningful changes to how transmission projects are planned, approved, and built, the United States risks a prolonged infrastructure shortfall. The researchers warn that failing to resolve these problems could weaken electricity reliability and inflict lasting damage on the national economy, even as demand for power continues to climb.

#133395. Tech Report: A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1598 w)

Tech Report: A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open fresh possibilities for quantum technology.
  • Industry observers note that the material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented.
  • Industry observers note that the discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open fresh possibilities for quantum technology. Researchers have found compelling evidence of a rare magnetic state in which electrons behave in unexpected ways, even though the material produces no overall magnetization.

Industry observers note that the material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented. This behavior is associated with a phenomenon called p-wave magnetism, an emerging area of research that could eventually help scientists develop newly introduced approaches to controlling electronic properties.

Industry observers note that the discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound. Unlike many materials previously considered for studying this exotic form of magnetism, it offers researchers a practical way to investigate the underlying physics in detail.

An Unexpected Discovery in a Simple Metal.

The research began about three years ago at the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids (MPI CPfS) in Dresden, Germany. Dr. Erjian Cheng successfully grew high-quality single crystals of EuSi, providing the material needed for detailed experiments.

Sources indicate that when researchers first examined the crystals using photoemission techniques, which probe the energies and behavior of electrons inside materials, they noticed something unexpected. The magnetic arrangement of the atoms had a remarkably strong influence on the electronic band structure, which describes the energy levels electrons can occupy and helps determine how a material conducts electricity.

According to recent reports, that observation raised an intriguing possibility. Could this simple compound contain an unconventional form of magnetism in which the spin of an electron is connected to the direction it travels?

Industry observers note that "When we first measured the electronic structure of EuSi, we were surprised by the exceptionally large effect of magnetism on the electrons," explains Cheng. "That observation led us to investigate whether this simple compound could host a much more unusual magnetic state. The combination of crystal growth, neutron scattering and spin-resolved spectroscopy now provides compelling evidence for p-wave magnetism.".

Sources indicate that answering that question required an international collaboration involving 38 scientists from 19 institutions. Participants included researchers from ShanghaiTech University, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, the Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

A Strange Form of Magnetism That Cancels Itself Out.

Ordinary magnets, such as those attached to refrigerators, typically rely on a magnetic arrangement called ferromagnetism. In these materials, many electron spins align in the same direction, producing an overall magnetic field.

At temperatures between approximately 33 and 62 kelvin, the magnetic moments of its europium atoms organize themselves into a repeating spiral pattern. These temperatures correspond to roughly minus 400 to minus 348 degrees Fahrenheit.

Each europium atom has a substantial magnetic moment, but their orientations balance one another across the spiral. As a result, the material has no net magnetization in this magnetic phase.

Sources indicate that however, the absence of overall magnetization does not mean magnetism has stopped influencing the electrons. In fact, the researchers found that the spiral arrangement produces a highly unusual electronic structure.

It has been revealed that in the proposed p-wave magnetic state, electrons traveling in opposite directions have opposite spin polarizations. Electron spin is a quantum property that gives electrons magnetic characteristics, although it should not be understood as an electron literally spinning like a tiny ball.

It has been revealed that the relationship between an electron's direction of motion and its spin is called an odd-parity spin texture. This means that reversing the electron's momentum also reverses the associated spin polarization.

Other materials can display spin-dependent energy differences because of a phenomenon known as spin-orbit coupling, which connects an electron's motion to its spin. In EuSi, however, the unusual spin structure appears to arise mainly from interactions between magnetic moments and the specific symmetry of their spiral arrangement.

Experiments Reveal Evidence of Rare P-Wave Magnetism.

To determine whether EuSi truly exhibits the predicted magnetic state, the scientists combined several sophisticated experimental methods with theoretical calculations.

First, they used neutron diffraction, a technique that reveals how atoms and magnetic moments are arranged inside a material. These measurements confirmed that the europium magnetic moments form a spiral structure with the symmetry required for p-wave magnetism.

Next, the researchers examined the material using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. This method measures the energies and momenta of electrons, allowing scientists to map the electronic structure.

The results indicated that magnetic ordering substantially reorganizes the electron energy levels. In particular, the team observed magnetically driven energy separations exceeding 100 millielectronvolts, indicating an unusually strong influence of magnetism on electron behavior.

The most decisive evidence came from spin-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which allowed the researchers to examine electron spin polarization directly.

Industry observers note that they observed that the sign of the spin polarization changed across successive magnetic Brillouin zones. These zones are regions of momentum space used by physicists to describe how electrons behave within a repeating magnetic structure.

The team also found that spin polarization became much weaker near locations where theoretical calculations predicted the p-wave spin texture should disappear.

Taken together, the measurements provide compelling experimental evidence consistent with the predicted p-wave magnetic state in EuSi.

A Hidden Magnetic Spiral With Two Different Orientations.

The researchers uncovered another unusual feature of EuSi involving chirality, a scientific term describing handedness.

Sources indicate that A familiar example is the difference between a left hand and a right hand. They are mirror images, but they cannot be perfectly superimposed.

Something similar happens with the magnetic spiral inside EuSi. Although the underlying crystal has a centrosymmetric structure, meaning its atomic arrangement is unchanged by inversion through a central point, the magnetic spiral can twist in either of two opposite directions.

These different spiral orientations create magnetic regions, or domains, with opposite handedness.

Sources indicate that using magnetic force microscopy and spatially resolved photoemission spectroscopy, the scientists identified domains measuring approximately ten micrometers across. For perspective, ten micrometers is about one-tenth the thickness of a typical human hair.

When the researchers examined these regions using circularly polarized light, they detected different electronic responses depending on the handedness of the magnetic spiral.

This finding demonstrates that the direction in which the magnetic structure twists is linked to the material's electronic properties.

It has been revealed that "What makes EuSi particularly exciting is that an unconventional electronic spin structure emerges from the magnetic order of a chemically simple metal," says Prof. Claudia Felser, Director at MPI CPfS. "This demonstrates how the discovery of newly introduced materials can reveal entirely new electronic phenomena. EuSi now gives us an experimental platform to investigate how magnetic symmetry and chirality can be used to control electronic properties, with potential implications for future spintronics and unconventional superconductivity.".

Why This Discovery Matters for Quantum Technology.

One of the biggest challenges in studying p-wave magnetism has been finding materials that display the necessary magnetic properties while remaining practical for detailed experiments.

Earlier candidates have included insulating materials, as well as metals that develop the required magnetic order only at extremely low temperatures or have complicated symmetries that make their behavior difficult to interpret.

EuSi offers a particularly useful combination of characteristics.

It is a stoichiometric metal, meaning its constituent elements occur in a fixed chemical ratio. Researchers can also grow high-quality single crystals of the material, and its spiral magnetic arrangement has the symmetry associated with p-wave magnetism.

Together, these features make EuSi a promising experimental platform for exploring how exotic magnetic states influence the behavior of electrons.

Sources indicate that theoretical studies suggest that metallic p-wave magnets could display several remarkable properties. For example, they may allow electrons with particular spin orientations to carry electrical currents without requiring an external magnetic field.

They could also produce strong changes in spin polarization when an electric current is applied, potentially offering upcoming ways to manipulate electronic behavior.

These possibilities are especially relevant to spintronics, a field of technology that seeks to use electron spin, rather than electrical charge alone, to process and store information.

Another intriguing possibility involves unconventional superconductivity, in which electrical current flows without resistance through superconducting states that differ from those found in conventional superconductors.

It has been revealed that importantly, these predicted effects have not yet been demonstrated in EuSi. The discovery does not establish that the material can already perform these functions, but it gives researchers a promising system in which to test the predictions.

More broadly, the findings highlight how much of a material's behavior can remain hidden beneath an apparently simple chemical composition.

Industry observers note that A solid's properties depend on more than the elements it contains or how its atoms are positioned. The arrangement of magnetic moments, the symmetries they create, and the quantum behavior of electrons can also produce entirely unexpected effects.

By revealing compelling evidence of p-wave magnetism in EuSi, researchers have gained a new opportunity to investigate these relationships and explore how unusual magnetic structures might eventually be used to control the electronic properties of future materials.

8 Things You Must Do Before Ending Chapter One in GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.
  • Note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6. You can deep sea dive for treasure, hang out with friends, complete missions, set up for Lucia, and a lot more. However, some of this absolutely needs to be done before you hit the end of the first chapter.

After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.

Note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game. There will also be spoilers ahead about chapter one.

Industry observers note that jason and Lucia have a chance to be madly in love in the beginning of the game. If you prepare for Lucia to get out of prison, work on Jason’s appearance, and focus on how they interact with each other, it will build a solid foundation.

In a recent development, there is a hard reset that comes at the end of the first chapter, and for a while, Lucia will be on her own while Jason recovers. With that being said, it will take a bit of a toll on their relationship.

This means that if you raise it up very high in the beginning, you won’t need to worry about needing to rebuild it as much later in the game, saving you a bit of time later on.

In a recent development, immediately after setting up your BuckMe account, you are told that you need to start saving money. The first goal in the game is to have a total savings of $5,000 stashed away. This is a pretty easy goal to hit, especially since there are a fair number of money-making opportunities in the first chapter.

You want to make sure that you hit this goal, as when the hard reset comes at the end of the chapter, you will lose everything except what is in your savings account.

As an added bonus, putting money away into your savings account will also raise your relationship, so it is a win-win situation. After you have everything saved up, the rest of your money is stuff you can play with.

Sources indicate that now that you have saved up the necessary cash for your family savings account, you might have some money burning a hole in your pocket. It is time to go on a bit of a shopping spree.

Sources indicate that as I said, you won’t be able to take this money with you into chapter two, so you will want to spend all of it. Buy some clothes, and definitely upgrade your weapons.

There is no point in upgrading your car, as you will lose this after chapter one. Instead, focus on increasing your wardrobe and upgrading your weapons as these will carry over into the next chapter.

There are some missions that you only have access to in the first chapter, and some of them belong to Shirley - Jason’s neighbor. She is a kind lady, and she will occasionally ask you to complete a few tasks.

These consist of getting her some alcohol, and stealing a mobility scooter from a lady nearby. They are fun short missions that you can complete within a few minutes, but they are worth doing because they are quite fun.

In a recent development, don’t worry about the treasure hunting, as you will be able to come back to it later on. Only certain missions disappear after the first chapter.

Industry observers note that there’s tons of details in GTA 6, which means that there are a bunch of collectibles that you can find scattered about. Some of these collectibles are books and magazines, and several of them are found around Jason’s house.

It has been revealed that before you end chapter one, you will want to get the books around Jason’s house. These include one in the bedroom, two in the living room, a magazine on the back deck, and one in the shed. Each of these disappears after the first chapter.

Recent findings suggest that along with this, you will want to grab the sunglasses in Donny’s trailer. You will make your way over there during one of the missions in the first chapter, so you shouldn’t miss out on them, but make sure to pick them up while you have the chance.

Sources indicate that if you have been focused on upgrading your weapons, gathering clothes, and putting money into your savings, then you will probably need some extra cash in the first chapter. Instead of searching for treasure, you should instead focus on completing the lost drug missions.

Recent findings suggest that there are four lost drug missions around Key Lento and up to the Grassrivers. These are special missions that end up disappearing after chapter one ends, so you will not have the ability to go back and complete them later on.

Since this is the only time you have access to them, you may as well complete them for the extra cash and spend it on stuff that will help you later in the game.

Recent findings suggest that while I have already established that buying weapons is important because they carry over, it is also important to grab the unique weapons that are obtainable early in the game. There are a couple weapons that you can find around the islands in Key Lento, and they will carry you in later parts of the game.

For instance, the Assassin Pistol can be found on a small dinghy on an island and it is great for completing missions stealthily in later parts of the game, and it has become one of my go-to weapons for staying hidden.

It has been revealed that there is also a shotgun that you can find that is quite powerful. It gets outclassed by other unique weapons later on, but it is great to have in chapter two.

In a recent development, one thing that is nice about GTA 6 is that it gives you the option to manually save. This means that you can create save points at key points in the game so that you can return to them later on.

I highly recommend completing what you can in chapter one and then creating a save point right before you go to do the tourist trap mission, as this is the last mission of the chapter, and it is also the point of no return.

If you want to play the game over but don’t want to deal with the slower pacing of the first chapter, you can skip all of that with a save right before the chapter change.

Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup. The move pairs him again with former NRG teammate brawk as Sentinels try to return to international events after missing them all in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Sources indicate that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and noted keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

In a recent development, the signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

Sources indicate that that spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko noted on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a newly introduced team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap quickly.

keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

In a recent development, the newly introduced lineup’s next test is the Americas Kickoff. Partner teams are guaranteed a place only at Kickoff. The Americas has eight partner teams, and all of them receive direct invitations to its event. Four further places go to non-partner teams.

In a recent development, the 2027 Kickoff events will be played in person in each international region. One of the non-partner places in the Americas will be decided by a Last Chance Qualifier in São Paulo on 17–18 December.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Car and Driver’s Testing Hub, where we zoom in on the test numbers. We’ve been pushing vehicles to their limits since 1956 to provide objective data to bolster our subjective impressions (you can see how we test here).

Sources indicate that the debut of the 2026 Lexus ES brought a full overhaul to the luxury sedan, which included a revamped hybrid variant. The new generation comes with fresh styling, a longer wheelbase, and an updated powertrain. In our testing, a 2026 ES350h was considerably quicker than a 2023 Lexus ES300h F Sport Handling, which was the last ES hybrid we tested.

See all results for new 2026 Lexus ES for sale near 92649.

Industry observers note that in our recent test of the ES350h, the updated sedan sprinted to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds, while the 2023 car more or less jogged its way to the 60-mph mark in 7.9 seconds. That’s a huge improvement, and one that took us by surprise, given that the upcoming car doesn’t look drastically more powerful than the old one on paper. That’s to say nothing of the additional 352 pounds of weight in the new car either.

So, where did all the extra quickness come from? Well, we can think of several places. For starters, the 2026 ES hybrid is more powerful, even if the numbers don’t jump off the page. The powertrain, which features a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, now churns out 244 horsepower, up from 215 in the 2023 ES. Along with a more powerful engine, the updated hybrid system uses a larger and more powerful electric drive motor than the previous generation. Lexus also now offers the gas-electric ES with all-wheel drive for the first time, and that’s the version we tested, with the additional traction helping offset the upcoming car’s weight gain.

According to recent reports, the latest generation also moved from a 3.39:1 axle ratio to a 3.44:1 axle ratio, a change that increases low-end torque at the wheels and makes the newer car somewhat punchier off the line. Lastly, the 2026 car gets a larger hybrid battery that can provide more horsepower than the smaller unit in the previous ES.

None of the changes are individually earth-shattering—especially with the extra 352 pounds of weight—but add them together, and the ES hybrid is a much quicker car than before.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty newly introduced for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Recent findings suggest that another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

It has been revealed that the demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#133389. Cannabis owners develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Cannabis owners develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug.
  • It has been revealed that the findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney.
  • Sources indicate that psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

It has been revealed that the findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

Sources indicate that psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood.

According to recent reports, to investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

Sources indicate that in studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis users experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

It has been revealed that the largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis customers experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age.

Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, noted the findings raise crucial questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

"We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large said. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine.".

Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis people and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

However, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis owners face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

Sources indicate that "There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large noted.

Sources indicate that the researchers also stressed an vital limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

Nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

"But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis.".

New Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25.

The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

Industry observers note that in a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis users. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

By incorporating a much larger body of research, the new analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, noted the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

Industry observers note that "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens noted.

"There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is notable, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone.".

Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter.

Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

Sources indicate that the late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these notable milestones.

"People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens said.

Prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

Industry observers note that "It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he stated. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline.".

The potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings.

Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

Sources indicate that "We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large said. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met.".

It has been revealed that one concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large mentioned its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

"It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk.".

Another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

Recent findings suggest that "You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large remarked.

More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure.

The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis owners, an increasingly important population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

Sources indicate that another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, the fresh analysis highlights an important gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

Materials provided by University of New South Wales. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

It has been revealed that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

It has been revealed that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Latest Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Newly introduced Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

In a recent development, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

Industry observers note that this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

According to recent reports, although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.
